alt.en: A detail of an old printed page. A paragraph reads "Come boys, lend a hand here! Man the capstan-bars! Give us a song now! Old Dave is our 'chanty-man.' Tune up, David!" Below it is a verse beginning "O Shannydore, I long to hear you!", with lines marked Chorus and Full Chorus, ending "On the wild Atlantic!"
alt.es: Detalle de una página impresa antigua. Un párrafo dice "Come boys, lend a hand here! Man the capstan-bars! Give us a song now! Old Dave is our 'chanty-man.' Tune up, David!" Debajo hay una estrofa que empieza "O Shannydore, I long to hear you!", con versos marcados Chorus y Full Chorus, y que termina "On the wild Atlantic!"

caption.en: "Shannydore" in The Riverside Magazine for Young People, April 1868, page 185: the song's earliest known printing, led by old Dave at the capstan, with the crew singing of the Atlantic, not the Missouri.
caption.es: "Shannydore" en The Riverside Magazine for Young People, abril de 1868, página 185: la primera impresión conocida de la canción, dirigida por el viejo Dave en el cabrestante, con la tripulación cantando al Atlántico, no al Missouri.

source: "Sailors' Songs" (unsigned), The Riverside Magazine for Young People, vol. 2, no. 16 (April 1868), p. 185, detail of the left column ("Come boys, lend a hand here!" and the first verse of "Shannydore")
licenceEvidence: Printed in the April 1868 issue (running head "1868.] Sailors' Songs. 185"); the article is unsigned. Published in the US before 1931; an anonymous work's EU and Israeli term (70 years from publication) ended in 1938. A faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: The Riverside Magazine for Young People, April 1868, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music, page 20, headed "9. Shenandoah" and "(Windlass and Capstan.)", marked "Slowly and with much expression", with staves for violin, voice and piano. Under the voice part, marked Solo and then Chorus, are the words "1. Oh Shenandoah, I long to hear you. A-way you rolling".
alt.es: Página impresa de música, página 20, con el encabezado "9. Shenandoah" y "(Windlass and Capstan.)", marcada "Slowly and with much expression", con pentagramas para violín, voz y piano. Bajo la voz, marcada Solo y luego Chorus, están las palabras "1. Oh Shenandoah, I long to hear you. A-way you rolling".

caption.en: Shenandoah as No. 9 of Richard Runciman Terry's The Shanty Book, Part I (London, 1921), among the windlass and capstan shanties: our tune is his, note for note.
caption.es: Shenandoah como n.º 9 de The Shanty Book, Part I de Richard Runciman Terry (Londres, 1921), entre las canciones marineras de molinete y cabrestante: nuestra melodía es la suya, nota por nota.

source: Richard Runciman Terry, The Shanty Book, Part I: Sailor Shanties (London: J. Curwen & Sons, 1921), No. 9, "Shenandoah (Windlass and Capstan)", p. 20
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: M1977 .S2 T4; Internet Archive shantybooksailor00terr, scan image n41
licenceEvidence: Published London 1921; editor and arranger Richard Runciman Terry 1865-1938 (IA record "Terry, Richard Runciman, 1865-1938"). US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: life + 70 ended 31 December 2008. The tune and words are traditional. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a wide, shallow river under a pale sky, with sandbars and a long island of reeds and bushes stretching to a flat horizon. Tall grass and bushes cover the near bank, where a woman in a dark dress and hat stands at the left beside a saddled horse.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de un río ancho y poco profundo bajo un cielo pálido, con bancos de arena y una isla alargada de juncos y arbustos que se extiende hasta un horizonte llano. Hierba alta y arbustos cubren la orilla cercana, donde a la izquierda hay una mujer con vestido oscuro y sombrero junto a un caballo ensillado.

caption.en: The wide Missouri near the Omaha Indian Agency, photographed by William Henry Jackson in 1869: the river the song crosses in its later versions, printed from 1876 on.
caption.es: El ancho Missouri cerca de la Omaha Indian Agency, fotografiado por William Henry Jackson en 1869: el río que la canción cruza en sus versiones posteriores, impresas desde 1876.

source: Missouri River near Omaha Indian Agency. Mrs. W.H. Jackson in foreground. (photograph by William Henry Jackson, 1869; series: Hayden Survey, William H. Jackson, Photographs, 1869-1878)
library: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration, Still Picture Branch, College Park (Record Group 57, Records of the U.S. Geological Survey)
licenceEvidence: NARA catalogue record 516607: use restriction "Unrestricted", access restriction "Unrestricted"; photographer "Jackson, William Henry, 1843-1942"; date 1869. Life + 70 ended 31 December 2012, so PD in the US (published or not), the EU and Israel (see rights.md).
